senses.gloss: f. (δελφική = δέλφιξ, delphica, sub. mensa) delphica, a three-legged table used as a toilet table or a waiter, contrad. fr. שלחן eating table (v. Becker Gallus, ed. Göll II, p. 354).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 22:1">Ib. XXII, 1</cite>; <cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Batra 1:9">Tosef. Kel. B. Bath. I, 9</cite> <he>דולפני</he> (corr. acc.).
<cite ref="Mishnah Avodah Zarah 5:5">Ab. Zar. V, 5</cite> (<cite ref="Avodah Zarah 69a">69ᵃ</cite>) <he>דלפ׳</he> Ar. (Ms. M. <he>דלוב׳</he>, ed. <he>דולב׳</he>, v. Rabb. D. S. a. l. note).

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Demai 6:7:2">Y. Dem. VI, 25ᵈ</cite> statuary made <he>כמין ד׳</he> like a kind of delphica (for practical use and not for idol worship, cmp. <cite ref="B00997"><he>בָּסִיס</he></cite>). *<cite ref="Shemot Rabbah 43:7">Ex. R. s. 43</cite> <he>מגפפת לד׳</he> hugging the statuary figure supporting a delphica (<cite ref="Bamidbar Rabbah 2">Num. R. s. 2</cite> <cite ref="O01620"><he>סריס</he></cite>).—Pl. <he>דְּלִפְקִיּוֹת</he>. Y. Ab. Zar. III, 42ᶜ bot.
